correctness.rationale: The unrestricted k-pebble strategy preserves coordinatewise equality patterns and uses only the exact fresh-symbol cutoff k. The converse defines intrinsic edges by containment in cliques of sizes 2 through k; pure-colour component diameters recover the multiplicity of each truncated factor order with only k variable names. The k=1 and k=2 cases, fixed-d theory census, and sharp isolation width follow from separate proofs. The embedded checker passed 392 finite single-coordinate extension cases and 90 independently reconstructed coloured-diameter cases; these corroborate rather than replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The result gives the full multiset classification at every variable width across arbitrarily many heterogeneous complete factors. Closest earlier results cover uniform Hamming factors or only two rook factors, or establish graph embeddings or counting-WL structure rather than this counting-free equivalence. The new ingredient is intrinsic logical recovery of the count of factors in each truncated size class via clique-coloured component diameters. Search coverage is non-exhaustive and possible subsumption by a general product theorem is a documented risk.
residual_risks: The classification may be an unrecognized corollary of a general pebble-game composition theorem for Cartesian products of cliques, not found in the checked sources.
Historical literature search is not exhaustive; unindexed older treatments of mixed-alphabet Hamming graphs may contain equivalent assertions.
Only bounded samples of the algebraic extension rule and coloured diameter reconstruction were computed. The infinite conclusion depends on the written proof.

value.rationale: Complete classification for an infinite natural family of rectangular Hamming graphs with unrestricted factor count, mixed alphabets and arbitrary bounded-variable width. The theorem supplies a canonical truncated-factor multiset invariant, an exact finite-dimension theory count and an optimal logical isolation-width formula. Unlike elementary fixed-factor examples, the argument logically recovers the multiplicity of every factor-size class using a fixed number of variables despite unbounded number of factors; this is independently motivated by the loss of counting information in finite-variable logic.
